scenes.say: ARIA roles and attributes boost accessibility, but only when native HTML can't do the job. So, when should you reach for ARIA?

scenes.label: Dialog
scenes.say: Use ARIA roles like dialog to explain custom widgets, such as modals, to assistive tech.
ARIA attributes clarify state and purpose. For example, aria-label names, aria-checked signals state, and aria-live triggers screen reader updates.
Always pick native HTML first. Only use ARIA roles when native elements can't provide the right semantics.

scenes.question: Should you add ARIA to every element?
scenes.right: No, misuse can confuse assistive tech. Use ARIA only when needed.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: adding ARIA everywhere. That actually harms accessibility. Use ARIA only when native HTML falls short.
